correction.text: unchanged, 1363–1401

correction.text: Champa 'reduced to Panduranga' south of the Cù Mông Pass: Kauthara and Panduranga, the border at Cù Mông 'from 1471 till 1611'

Cliopatria's 1475 shape (8,027 km2) covers only Khánh Hòa and Ninh Thuận; the four provinces south of Cù Mông are about 21,000 km2 of lowland. The highland rump ('one in the Central Highlands') that 'submitted to Thánh Tông as vassals' is not drawn.

correction.text: Champa 'reduced to Panduranga' south of the Cù Mông Pass: Kauthara and Panduranga, the border at Cù Mông 'from 1471 till 1611'

correction.text: Kauthara and Panduranga after the Nguyễn took Phú Yên in 1611

correction.text: Kauthara and Panduranga after the Nguyễn took Phú Yên in 1611

correction.text: Kauthara and Panduranga after the Nguyễn took Phú Yên in 1611

keyframe_review.note: Same 7,917 km2 shape; use champa_1611 (Khánh Hòa, Ninh Thuận, Bình Thuận) to 1652. Cliopatria ends Champa in 1652; the state continued as Panduranga to 1832.

correction.text: Panduranga (Phan Rang and Phan Rí), the last Cham land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'the Kauthara principality was lost to the Nguyen after a counterattack in 1653' (Champa page: '1653: Kauthara was annexed by the Vietnamese'); Panduranga alone remains, to the 1692 invasion and the 1694 restoration.

correction.text: Panduranga (Phan Rang and Phan Rí), the last Cham land

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Thuận Thành, 'From 1695 onward, Panduranga had been reduced to a client state of the Nguyen domain', confirmed by 'a following treaty signed in 1712', to the 1832 annexation. The vassal tint over these years belongs to the Nguyễn lords (to 1775) and Nguyễn dynasty dossiers (notes).

region.text: Tượng Lâm (Xianglin) county, 'modern-day Huế city'

ledger.note: 192: Khu Liên rebels against the Han and founds Lâm Ấp at Tượng Lâm. 'led a successful rebellion against the Han dynasty in Tượng Lâm (Xianglin) county (modern-day Huế city) in 192.' The Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư dates the rising to 137; Cliopatria's first shape begins 207.

region.text: 'most of Rinan': the coast north of Huế to the Quảng Bình line

ledger.note: 248: Lâm Ấp seizes most of Rinan. 'In 248, Lâm Ấp force invaded from the south, seized most of Rinan'; the land is read as the coast north of Huế to the Quảng Bình line, as Cliopatria's 207 shape draws it. Eastern Wu held Jiaozhou in 248.

region.text: Rinan north of the Gianh to the Hoành Sơn range

ledger.note: 347: Fan Wen attacks Jin Jiaozhou; Lâm Ấp's frontier is afterwards placed at the Hoành Sơn range. 'In 347, king Fan Wen (范文) attacked Jin-controlled Jiaozhou with 40–50,000 troops.' The page gives the attack, not the frontier; Quảng Bình to Hoành Sơn is the researcher's reading, matching Cliopatria's 546 shape. Cliopatria's 'Western Jin' row covers the Eastern Jin of 347.

region.text: Lâm Ấp's capital (near modern Huế)

ledger.note: 446: Tan Hezhi's Liu Song army takes and plunders the Lâm Ấp capital. 'In February 446, the Liu Song dynasty led by Tan Hezhi invaded Lâm Ấp, captured Lâm Ấp's capital' and 'plundered its eight temples and treasury, carrying off 100,000 pounds of gold'. Hatched (rule 4), no change of owner; the page's massacre ('more than half of Lâm Ấp's people were slaughtered') is dated 420.

region.text: Lâm Ấp's capital (near modern Huế)

ledger.note: 446: the Song army withdraws with its plunder. The page gives no date for the withdrawal and records no annexation.

region.text: 'the Cham capital of Trà Kiệu'

ledger.note: 605: Liu Fang's Sui army takes Trà Kiệu. 'In 605 Yang Chien ordered Liu Fang to invade Lâm Ấp'; 'Chinese troops captured the Cham capital of Trà Kiệu, plundered the city'. Hatched, no change of owner.

region.text: Trà Kiệu

ledger.note: 605: the Sui withdraw. The page records the plunder, not a garrison; the year of withdrawal is the researcher's reading.
629: the state calls itself Champa. 'Since 629, the Chams had used the name "Champa"'; infobox 'Becoming Champa: 629'. Same state, same colour (rule 2).
757: the Panduranga dynasty takes the throne of Champa. 'a new southern dynasty, called Panduranga, rose in 757'. Same state, same colour.
757: the capital moves south to Virapura near Phan Rang (infobox: Virapura 757–875; Panduranga page: 'established its capital at Virapura, also known as Palai Bachong').

region.text: Kauthara and Panduranga, the coast from Nha Trang to Phan Rí

ledger.note: 757: the southern coast, Kauthara and Panduranga, is drawn as Champa from the Panduranga dynasty's accession. Cliopatria adds it only in 875; the pages opened do not say who held it before (Kauthara is first named in an inscription of 784, Panduranga in 817: Champa page). 'nobody' here means no Cliopatria row: these were Cham principalities, not stateless land.

758: the Chinese call the state Huanwang (Hoàn Vương). '758–809: Chinese texts refer to the whole of Champa as Huánwáng'; the Lâm Ấp page: 'From the mid-8th century, Chinese xenonym for Champa had changed from Linyi to Huánwáng'.

region.text: Nghệ An (the Tang Hoan Prefecture, today Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh)

ledger.note: 803: Champa seizes Nghệ An from the Tang. 'Champa seized Nghệ An from the Tang' (803). The region is the Tang Hoan Prefecture, read as today's Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh.

region.text: Nghệ An (the Tang Hoan Prefecture, today Nghệ An and Hà Tĩnh)

ledger.note: 809: the Tang recover Nghệ An. 'The Chinese recovered the lost regions' (809).

875: Indravarman II moves the capital to Indrapura. 'In 875, a new Buddhist dynasty founded by Indravarman II (r. ? – 893) moved the capital or the major center of Champa to the north again'; 'Indravarman II established the city of Indrapura, near My Son and ancient Simhapura'; 'Art historians often attribute the period between 875 and 982 as the Golden Age of Champa art'.

region.text: northern Champa around Indrapura

ledger.note: 982: Lê Hoàn's Vietnamese invasion devastates northern Champa. 'Lê Hoàn led a Vietnamese invasion that brought mass destruction to northern Champa' (982); the Vietnamese Lưu Kế Tông 'took the throne' in 983 and reigned 986–989 at Indrapura. Hatched: Cliopatria's Ngô Dynasty row is the Early Lê state of 982.
982: the court moves south to Vijaya (infobox: Vijaya 982–1471). The body text keeps Indrapura as capital to about 1100, a disagreement within the page.

region.text: northern Champa around Indrapura

ledger.note: 989: the end of Lưu Kế Tông's reign at Indrapura ('986–989') closes the Vietnamese presence in the north; the year is the researcher's reading of the reign dates.

region.text: the three areas Địa Lý, Ma Linh and Bố Chính, which 'now form part of Quảng Bình Province and Quảng Trị Province' ('Quảng Bình and northern part of Quảng Trị Provinces', Nam tiến page)

ledger.note: 1069: Rudravarman III buys his freedom with Địa Lý, Ma Linh and Bố Chính. 'in 1069 Lý Thánh Tông himself led an seaborne invasion of Champa', 'burned Vijaya, and captured the king of Champa, Rudravarman III'; 'Rudravarman III implored Lý Thánh Tông to release him in exchange for three areas, known as Địa Lý, Ma Linh, and Bố Chính', which 'now form part of Quảng Bình Province and Quảng Trị Province'. Cliopatria moves the border in 1072.

region.text: Vijaya and 'northern Champa'

ledger.note: 1145: Suryavarman II sacks Vijaya and occupies northern Champa. 'turned to invade Champa in 1145 and sacked Vijaya'; the temples at Mỹ Sơn were destroyed. Hatched (rule 4).

region.text: Vijaya and northern Champa

ledger.note: 1149: Jaya Harivarman I retakes Vijaya. 'Harivarman marched his army northward to Vijaya' and the campaign 'ended Suryavarman's occupation of northern Champa'.

region.text: 'the Khmer capital of Yasodharapura' and the Tonlé Sap heartland

ledger.note: 1177: the Cham fleet sacks Angkor. The Cham 'launched a surprise attack against the Khmer capital of Yasodharapura' (June 1177, Champa page), beginning 'the Cham occupation of Cambodia for the next four years'. Hatched over the Khmer heartland.

region.text: the Khmer heartland

ledger.note: 1181: Jayavarman VII expels the Cham. His forces 'had rescued the empire and expelled the Cham' (1181).

region.text: Vijaya

ledger.note: 1190: a Khmer army under Vidyanandana occupies Vijaya; Panduranga becomes a Khmer vassal. He 'proceeded to occupy Vijaya' and made himself king of 'Panduranga, which became a Khmer vassal'.

region.text: Vijaya

ledger.note: 1191: Vidyanandana turns on his masters. After the revolt at Vijaya he 'reigned without opposition over the Kingdom of Champa', declaring independence from the Khmer Empire.

region.text: northern Champa around Vijaya, invaded in 1192, 1195, 1198–1199 and 1201–1203

ledger.note: 1192: Jayavarman VII's invasions of Champa begin. 'several invasions of Champa' in 1192, 1195, 1198–1199 and 1201–1203; the north around Vijaya is the fighting zone until the 1203 conquest.

region.text: northern Champa around Vijaya

ledger.note: 1203: the Khmer conquest completed. 'completing the Khmer conquest of Champa' (1203).

region.text: the whole of Champa, as Cliopatria's 1188 shape draws it

ledger.note: 1203: Champa becomes a Khmer province. 'Champa as a Khmer province was ruled by a puppet government' (1203). Cliopatria has no Champa shape 1206–1219; the Khmer Empire dossier should carry the matching gain.

region.text: the whole of Champa, as Cliopatria's 1220 shape draws it

ledger.note: 1220: the Khmer evacuate Champa. 'voluntary Khmer evacuation of Champa in 1220'; Angsaräja 'restored Champa's independence'.

region.text: Vijaya

ledger.note: 1283: the Mongols take Vijaya. 'Vijaya fell in February 1283' during the Yuan invasion of 1283–1285.

region.text: Vijaya

ledger.note: 1285: the Yuan repelled. 'the Mongols were repelled by June 1285'; 'the Yuan wars ended' in 1288.

region.text: the 'two provinces of Ô and Lý' (Thuận Hóa: Thừa Thiên and southern Quảng Trị)

ledger.note: 1306: Chế Mân cedes Ô and Lý for Princess Huyền Trân. 'Chế Mân ceded two provinces of Ô and Lý' (1306); the Champa page: 'Princess Huyền Trân's marriage to Prince Harijit was arranged in exchange for peace and territory'. Cliopatria moves the border in 1314.

region.text: Hóa Châu (Thừa Thiên, Quảng Trị), Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa, where Chế Bồng Nga held ground between 1376 and 1390

ledger.note: 1371: Chế Bồng Nga sacks Thăng Long; the war for Hóa Châu, Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa runs to 1390. 'Cham force sacked the Viet capital of Thăng Long' (1371); 'launched incursions into Hoá Châu' (1376); he 'sacked Hanoi in late 1377, gaining control of vast territories including Thanh Hoá and Nghệ An'; Hanoi taken again in 1378 and in 1383, 'occupying it for six months'. Blend (rule 6), no border change: 'Status quo ante bellum'.

region.text: Hóa Châu, Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa

ledger.note: 1390: Chế Bồng Nga killed. 'Chế Bồng Nga was killed in 1390 by firearms of Vietnamese Prince Trần Khát Chân' at the Hải Triều River, 'early 1390'; infobox result 'Champa defensive victory', 'no territorial changes'.

region.text: 'four regions Thăng, Hoa, Tư, and Nghĩa and Tân Ninh highlands': Quảng Nam and Quảng Ngãi

ledger.note: 1402: Indravarman VI cedes Chiêm Động and Cổ Lũy to the Hồ. The Hồ forced 'Indravarman VI to ceded four regions Thăng, Hoa, Tư, and Nghĩa and Tân Ninh highlands to the Dai Ngu' (1402); the four regions are read as Quảng Nam and Quảng Ngãi. Cliopatria's Ngô Dynasty row covers the Hồ state (Đại Ngu).

region.text: the four regions ceded in 1402

ledger.note: 1406: the four territories return to Champa as Đại Ngu falls to the Ming. 'Four former territories gained by Hồ Hán Thương were returned to Champa' (1406; the Nam tiến page's 1403 siege of Vijaya failed).

region.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

ledger.note: 1470: Lê Thánh Tông's expedition sails. 'On November 28, 1470, a 100,000-strong Vietnamese naval expedition' set out, 'followed by another 150,000 civilian support personnel on December 8', after 'a Cham army numbering 100,000 under King Maha Sajan arrived and besieged the Vietnamese garrison at Huế' in 1470.

region.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

ledger.note: 1471: Vijaya falls. 'Thánh Tông then converged his armies to surround the city of Vijaya (12 miles west of Thị Nại) on March 19'; 'On March 22, the city fell after a four-day siege'.

region.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

ledger.note: 1471: Champa loses everything north of the Cù Mông Pass. 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên) was annexed to Đại Việt'; 'king Thánh Tông established Quảng Nam as Đại Việt's 13th province'; 'the border between Đại Việt and Champa was moved from Hải Vân Pass to Cù Mông Pass'; 'More than 30,000 Chams were captured, including Trà Toàn', 'over 60,000 killed'.

1471: the Cham court is reduced to Panduranga (infobox: Panduranga polity 1471–1832); two other rulers, 'one in the Central Highlands and one on the coast south of Bình Định', 'subsequently submitted to Thánh Tông as vassals' (1471 war page).

region.text: the land between the Cù Mông and Cả passes

ledger.note: 1611: the Nguyễn take Phú Yên, the land between the Cù Mông and Cả passes. The 1611 attack 'sent under lord Nguyen Phuc Nguyen' is described as 'annexing the entire Kauthara Principality', but the same page has Kauthara 'lost to the Nguyen after a counterattack in 1653', so 1611 is read as Kauthara's northern part, Phú Yên; the 1471 page has the Cù Mông border hold 'from 1471 till 1611'.

region.text: the Kauthara principality around Nha Trang

ledger.note: 1653: Kauthara lost. 'the Kauthara principality was lost to the Nguyen after a counterattack in 1653'; Champa page: '1653: Kauthara was annexed by the Vietnamese'. Cliopatria ends Champa the year before.

region.text: Panduranga (Phan Rang and Phan Rí), the last Cham land

ledger.note: 1692: Nguyễn Phúc Chu invades Panduranga. 'In 1692, lord Nguyễn Phúc Chu invaded Panduranga, arresting King Po Saut and renaming Panduranga to Trấn Thuận Thành'. Hatched until the 1694 restoration.

region.text: Panduranga (Phan Rang and Phan Rí), the last Cham land

ledger.note: 1694: the Cham prince restored as King of Thuận Thành. 'Cham revolts in 1693–96 forced the Nguyen lord to mitigate the resentment'; 'In 1694, Panduranga king Po Saktiraydapatih (r. 1695–1727) received the title King of Thuan Thanh'; 'From 1695 onward, Panduranga had been reduced to a client state of the Nguyen domain', confirmed by 'a following treaty signed in 1712'. The vassal tint 1695–1832 belongs to the Nguyễn lords' and Nguyễn dynasty's dossiers.

region.text: Panduranga (Phan Rang and Phan Rí), the last Cham land

ledger.note: 1832: Minh Mạng annexes Panduranga. 'August 1832: Minh Mạng began his purge and deposed the last Cham king, Po Phaok The'; infobox: annexation of Panduranga November 1832; Nam tiến page: 'In 1832, the Emperor annexed Champa'. Panduranga's kings had been 'appointed by the Huế court' since 1799.

wars.name: Fan Wen's war with Jin (347)

zones.text: Rinan north of Huế to the Hoành Sơn range

wars.outcome: The page records only the attack: 'In 347, king Fan Wen (范文) attacked Jin-controlled Jiaozhou with 40–50,000 troops'; the usual account leaves Lâm Ấp at the Hoành Sơn range.
wars.note: The page lists 'Phạm Văn 336–349' among the kings; the war's end year 349 is that reign's end, not a dated battle.

wars.name: Liu Song campaign against Lâm Ấp (446)
wars.outcome: 'In February 446, the Liu Song dynasty led by Tan Hezhi invaded Lâm Ấp, captured Lâm Ấp's capital'; the capital was plundered and the army withdrew, no border moved.

wars.name: Sui–Lâm Ấp war (605)
wars.outcome: 'In 605 Yang Chien ordered Liu Fang to invade Lâm Ấp'; Trà Kiệu was captured and plundered; the Sui did not stay.

wars.name: Lê Hoàn's invasion of Champa (982)
wars.outcome: 'Lê Hoàn led a Vietnamese invasion that brought mass destruction to northern Champa'; the Vietnamese Lưu Kế Tông reigned at Indrapura 986–989; the Cham court moved to Vijaya.
wars.note: Cliopatria's 'Ngô Dynasty' row is the Vietnamese state of 982 (Early Lê).

wars.name: Khmer–Cham wars

zones.text: Vijaya and northern Champa, occupied 1145–1149 and 1190–1191, invaded 1192–1203
Yasodharapura and the Khmer heartland, held by the Cham 1177–1181
Kauthara, where the Khmer 'pillaged the temple of Po Nagar' in 950
all of Champa, a Khmer province 1203–1220

wars.outcome: 'lasted from the mid-10th century to the early 13th century'; Champa was a Khmer province from 1203 and 'The conflicts ended after the Khmer army voluntarily retreated from occupying Champa in 1220'.
wars.note: The 1128 and 1132 Khmer attacks on Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa were against Đại Việt, not Champa.

wars.name: Champa–Đại Việt War (1069)

zones.text: the three areas Địa Lý, Ma Linh and Bố Chính, which 'now form part of Quảng Bình Province and Quảng Trị Province' ('Quảng Bình and northern part of Quảng Trị Provinces', Nam tiến page)

wars.outcome: Lý Thánh Tông 'burned Vijaya, and captured the king of Champa, Rudravarman III'; the king was released 'in exchange for three areas, known as Địa Lý, Ma Linh, and Bố Chính'.
wars.note: The war's own article (Champa–Đại Việt War (1069)) would not load; the Lý Thánh Tông page carries the same facts.

wars.name: Mongol invasion of Champa (1283–1285)
wars.outcome: 'The Yuan invaded. Vijaya fell in February 1283, and the Mongols were repelled by June 1285'; no border moved.

wars.name: Champa–Đại Việt War (1367–1390)

zones.text: Hóa Châu, Nghệ An and Thanh Hóa, where Chế Bồng Nga held ground 1376–1390
Thăng Long, sacked in 1371, 1377, 1378 and 1383 (held six months)

wars.outcome: 'Champa defensive victory, Vietnamese invasion failed'; 'Status quo ante bellum as no territorial changes; Both states severely weakened'. Chế Bồng Nga was killed in early 1390.
wars.note: In 1377 'he killed emperor Trần Duệ Tông (r. 1373–1377) at the Battle of Vijaya'.

wars.name: Champa–Đại Việt War (1471)

zones.text: 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên)': the land between the Hải Vân and Cù Mông passes

wars.outcome: 'Đại Việt victory'; 'Northern Champa (now Quảng Nam, Quảng Ngãi and north of Phú Yên) was annexed to Đại Việt' and 'Champa was reduced to Panduranga'; the border moved 'from Hải Vân Pass to Cù Mông Pass'.
wars.note: 'In 1474, Bố Trì Trì rebelled against the Vietnamese' and 'After an expedition to Champa in 1446, Vietnamese efforts to hold the Cham king as a vassal quickly failed' are the page's earlier and later episodes.

wars.name: Nguyễn conquest of Panduranga (1692–1694)

zones.text: Panduranga (Phan Rang and Phan Rí), the last Cham land

wars.outcome: 'In 1692, lord Nguyễn Phúc Chu invaded Panduranga, arresting King Po Saut and renaming Panduranga to Trấn Thuận Thành'; after the revolts of 1693–96 the Cham king was restored as 'King of Thuan Thanh' (1694) and 'From 1695 onward, Panduranga had been reduced to a client state of the Nguyen domain'.

certainty.note: Mandala frontiers; the Hoành Sơn range as the northern limit from the 4th century is a named range, everything else approximate. The inland limit toward the highlands is unknown throughout.
The cessions of 1069 (Địa Lý, Ma Linh, Bố Chính) and 1306 (Ô, Lý) are district lines nameable from the pages but not surveyed; the Hải Vân Pass is the northern limit 1306–1470.
The Cù Mông Pass border 1471–1611 and the Cả Pass after 1611 are named lines; Panduranga's limits toward the highlands and toward Nguyễn Bình Thuận after 1695 are approximate.

notes:
Cliopatria row 'Chámpa' 207–1652 (17 shapes) kept as one state: Lâm Ấp, Huanwang, Champa and Panduranga are one polity on the same land without a break (the infobox runs 192–1832), so the dynasty and name changes are rename events and no split is made. Corrections: start 192 (not 207); the realm reaches Panduranga from 757 (not 875); the 1069 and 1306 cessions dated from the pages (Cliopatria 1072 and 1314); no Champa shape 1203–1219 (a Khmer province; Cliopatria's gap 1206–1219 is close); the 1402–1405 cession of Quảng Nam and Quảng Ngãi added; Cliopatria's 1429 shape is wrong (Quảng Nam was Cham until 1471); the post-1471 shapes (8,000 km2) are far too small and replaced by province unions; the state continues as Panduranga/Thuận Thành to 1832 (Cliopatria ends 1652).

Low-confidence items a gap-filler should settle: the 347–349 Fan Wen war's outcome (Hoành Sơn frontier) from the 'Lâm Ấp' or 'Fan Wen' pages; the 4th-century border with Jin Rinan; the end of the Liu Song (446) and Sui (605) occupations within the year; who held Kauthara and Panduranga before 757 (treated as 'nobody' = no Cliopatria row); the 1044 Lý Thái Tông sack of Vijaya (not on the pages opened); the 1312–1326 Trần vassalage after the capture of Chế Chí; the 1446 Lê expedition; the exact year 1406 vs 1407 for the return of the four regions; 1611 read as Phú Yên although the Panduranga page says 'the entire Kauthara Principality'; the Cham rump 'in the Central Highlands' after 1471 (not drawn).

Pages that would not load: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Champa%E2%80%93%C4%90%E1%BA%A1i_Vi%E1%BB%87t_War_(1069) (replaced by Lý Thánh Tông).

Counterparts: the Vietnamese state of 982–1406 is Cliopatria's 'Ngô Dynasty' row (slug ngo-dynasty), used for the Early Lê, Lý, Trần and Hồ events; the Lê of 1471 is le-dynasty; the Nguyễn lords (1611, 1653, 1692) nguyen-lords; 1832 nguyen-dynasty; the Yuan of 1283 yuan-dynasty. Requests to other dossiers: khmer-empire should carry the gain of all Champa 1203–1220 and the occupations 1145–1149 and 1190–1191 (and the Cham occupation of Angkor 1177–1181 as a loss/occupation); ngo-dynasty should carry a vassal tint over Champa 1312–1326 and the 1069/1306/1402 gains; nguyen-lords should carry vassal_start 1695 (Thuận Thành) and nguyen-dynasty vassal_end/gain 1832. Disagreements between pages: capital Indrapura to 982 (infobox) or c. 1100 (body); Panduranga's capital Phan Rang to 1693 (infobox) or Phan Rí from the early 17th century (body); the 1832 annexation August (body) or November (infobox).

Gazetteer: all region names resolve (Natural Earth admin-1 spellings 'Quàng Nam', 'Thừa Thiên - Huế', 'Ha Tinh'; places Simhapura, Indrapura, Vijaya, Panduranga; region 'Angkor (region)').
